summary: The note describes "Move Your Mind," a community initiative launched September 5, 2023 by Andrea Mitchell that uses group fitness to promote mental wellness. It covers the science of exercise and mental health, a University study showing a 40% decrease in depression symptoms, participant stories, and inclusion efforts like "Wellness Without Barriers." Experts stress consistency and patience, and the initiative continues to grow with local business and health professional involvement.
one_line: The "Move Your Mind" community initiative uses group fitness, inclusion programs and education to improve mental wellness, backed by research on exercise's benefits.
key_facts: The "Move Your Mind" project, led by local fitness enthusiast Andrea Mitchell, launched on September 5, 2023 to promote holistic well-being through group fitness programs.
Andrea Mitchell is also the program director of "Move Your Mind" and spoke at a city hall meeting on September 29, 2023, saying group goals form connections that extend beyond physical health.

On September 15, psychologist Dr. Julian Torres told a community center gathering that exercise releases endorphins, the body's natural stress-relievers and mood lifters, and can reduce adrenaline and cortisol.
A University Psychology Department study released October 1, 2023 linked regular physical activity to better sleep, increased self-esteem and enhanced cognitive function.
In the University study, after six weeks of consistent group exercise participants reported a 40% decrease in symptoms of depression and a 30% increase in overall life satisfaction.
Local fitness clubs added more group classes, ranging from yoga to spin, HIIT to dance, suited to varied interests and ability levels.
Personal trainer Eric Turner, who recently moved to leading group sessions, says the social aspect of group workouts pushes people to accomplish more than they would alone.
Jenny Phillips, a mother of two struggling with postpartum depression, joined a local aerobics class through the initiative and shared her story at a wellness seminar on November 3.
On October 10, "Move Your Mind" introduced "Wellness Without Barriers," targeting older adults, people with disabilities and low-income families.
Former school teacher Linda Gomez, who has battled anxiety, has run free workshops since October 18 on using exercise to manage mental health issues.
Dr. Torres and fitness experts recommend realistic expectations and small, manageable increments of activity, as results are not instantaneous.
At a local run club meeting on November 17, members pledged to support one another's fitness goals.
Toward the end of the year, local businesses and health professionals are becoming increasingly involved in the initiative.
